config.grain_rationale: One record is one current Australian credit licence, identified by CRED_LIC_NUM, held by a legal person named in CRED_LIC_NAME (ASIC issues credit licences to legal entities). The business attributes mapped are those of the licensee/holder; the licence number, licence start date and licence status are attributes of the licence, not of the entity, so they are not mapped as business identifiers or entity.status.

record_id.rationale: CRED_LIC_NUM has present_rate 1.0 and 464 distinct values across 464 discovery records, i.e. unique per licence record; it is the natural traceable key for the licence grain.

fields.rationale: Column is CRED_LIC_NAME on a credit licence register: the licence is issued to the named holder, and the publisher states licence names follow the business register. Values are registered-form names ('...PTY LTD', 'LIMITED'). Some holders are individuals (e.g. 'TAN, JINTANG'), expected for sole-trader licensees; the field remains the registered legal name of the licensee, not a trading name.

CRED_LIC_BN is the licence's business name field, present on 34.5% of rows; values are short trading brands ('DISCOVERY FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT', 'STACKS FINANCE', 'PLANNING PARTNERS') distinct from the registered names in CRED_LIC_NAME. Business/brand names map to trading_name.

Combined ABN/ACN column: 420 of 464 discovery values are 11-digit checksum-valid ABNs. The regex_extract step restricts this rule to the 11-digit branch so the abn transform only ever sees ABN-shaped values; ACN-shaped, 7-8 digit and placeholder values produce no ABN observation instead of an error.

27 of 464 records carry a 9-digit ACN-shaped value in CRED_LIC_ABN_ACN; that branch is an ACN (the last 9 digits of an ABN are not always an ACN, so it is validated with the acn checksum, never derived). The regex_extract step selects only 9-digit values, so 11-digit ABNs, 7-8 digit values and the placeholder '0' are excluded from this field rather than erroring.
ASIC credit licensee extracts carry the licensee's locality/state/postcode as a group with latitude/longitude, i.e. the holder's contact address on the licence record.
All 464 values are already 2-3 letter AU state abbreviations over 8 distinct values (NSW, VIC, QLD, WA, SA, ACT, ...), consistent with the state enum.
All 464 values have shape 9999 (4-digit AU postcodes, e.g. 2000, 3000, 6102); normalised with the postcode transform.

constants.rationale: ASIC Australian credit licence register covering Australian licensees; all observed states are AU jurisdictions.

unmapped.reason: Constant register label ('Credit Licence') for every row; carries no entity attribute.
Identifier of the licence record, not of the business. Used only as record_id; the ontology has no licence field.

Date the credit licence started, not the entity's registration date (publisher evidence: grant/suspension/cancellation dates concern the licence). Mapping it to entity.date_registered would misstate company registration.
Dataset is 'Current' and the column is empty in every discovery row; also concerns licence end, not entity validity.
Status of the licence (single value 'APPR' = approved), not of the legal entity; licence status is not entity.status.
Free-text licence-condition contravention history (present on 0.2% of rows); describes the licence, not the entity.
Australian Financial Services licence number of the licensee, a licence identifier with no ontology target; 91.6% of values are the placeholder '0' anyway.
Latitude coordinate with no ontology address field for coordinates.
Longitude coordinate with no ontology address field for coordinates.
External dispute resolution scheme membership(s) of the licensee ('AFCA~FOS'); a compliance attribute, not an entity or address field.
Free-text description of what the licence authorises; describes licence scope, not the entity.

config.notes: Licence-grain register: record_id is the licence number, and licence dates/status are deliberately not mapped to entity fields. CRED_LIC_ABN_ACN is a mixed column - 420/464 are checksum-valid 11-digit ABNs, 27 are 9-digit ACN-shaped, 13 are the placeholder '0', and a few are 7-8 digits; each identifier rule is shape-guarded with regex_extract so the checksummed transforms only see values of the right length and invalid values yield no observation rather than an error. entity_type is left unmapped because no column states the business form explicitly (names ending in PTY LTD are not treated as a stated type). Address fields are the licensee's contact details on the licence record; the geography of the register does not by itself prove each record's location, but locality/state/postcode plus coordinates are presented as the licensee's address.

fields.reason: CRED_LIC_NAME on ASIC's credit licence register is the registered name of the licensee; values like 'RELI CAPITAL LTD', 'EDUCATED FINANCE PTY LTD', 'LUNAWAVE PTY. LIMITED' are registered forms, and personal-name entries ('TSIALTAS, ARGIRIOS HARRY', 'LATASH, EDDIE') come from the registered form 'SURNAME, GIVEN NAMES' style used for individual licensees rather than a contact person. The rationale explicitly notes licence names follow the business register. claim_scope current_legal_name fits; no unsupported validity bound is attached. The individual-name records are the licensee's registered name, so mapping to legal_name (not trading_name) is defensible; the only caveat is that entity_type is not derived from these forms (see missed).

CRED_LIC_BN carries distinct brand values ('FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE', 'KEYPLAYER FINANCE', 'DISCOVERY FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT') that differ from the registered names and are absent where no brand exists; mapping them to trading_name is correct, one observation per value. No alias or former-name assumption is made.

The 11-digit branch of the combined ABN/ACN column is validated with the abn checksum, and emitted values (80005443292, 24609333799, 55094972540, 19004493789, 51624785486, 14985946274, 33003565080) appear as ABNs. The regex_extract correctly rejects ACN-shaped, 7-8 digit and '0' placeholders (e.g. the '0' record and '102331359' produce no ABN), which matches the observed output.

The 9-digit branch is treated as an ACN and checksum-validated rather than derived from the ABN; emitted values ('102331359' for EDUCATED FINANCE PTY LTD, '601283201' for HEAJAS PTY LTD) look ACN-shaped and no ABN-derived ACN appears. 11-digit ABNs and '0' are excluded. Consistent with the source semantics.

CRED_LIC_LOCALITY is reasonably the licensee's address group (with state/postcode/lat/lng), but the mapping calls it licence_holder_address without publisher evidence: ASIC's credit licence extracts also contain licensed business/premises addresses, and the claim_scope asserts a specific address kind the supplied publisher evidence does not confirm. Values emitted (LEONGATHA, PENRITH, SYDNEY, BRUNSWICK, TEMPLESTOWE, WILEY PARK) are plausible, but the scope label is asserted rather than evidenced.

All emitted values (VIC, NSW, QLD) are 2-3 letter AU state abbreviations resolvable to the enum; no guess-driven assignment observed and no non-AU jurisdiction appears in the held-out rows. Same address-kind doubt as rule 4, but the state transform itself is correct.

All values are 4-digit AU postcodes (3953, 2750, 2000, 4870, 3056, 3205, 4017, 3175, 3106, 2195) matching their states; postcode transform and null_if are appropriate and no non-AU or malformed values are emitted.
Constant AU is supported: the register is ASIC's Australian credit licence register, all observed states are AU jurisdictions, and the publisher is ASIC. No NZ or OTHER evidence appears.

missed.source_path: CRED_LIC_NAME (registered-name form and suffix, e.g. 'PTY LTD', 'LIMITED', 'PTY. LIMITED', or 'SURNAME, GIVEN NAMES')
missed.reason: The dataset contains both company-style suffixes and individual licensee names, yet no entity_type observation is emitted. Deriving company from 'PTY LTD'/'LIMITED' suffixes and treating bare personal names cautiously (unknown or, at most, evidence-limited sole_trader) would use an actual source column; currently entity_type is simply absent. Note the rule must not guess: personal name alone is weak evidence, so 'unknown' is a safe output.

Only value 'APPR' is observed, so mapping it is arguable; but if the mapping were to use status at all it should be a licence-level caveat. Since the mapping deliberately excludes it and no entity-status source exists, this is correctly omitted — listing only to note that a licence approval does not evidence entity active status, so no status observation should be invented.

critic.summary: The mapping is largely sound: legal_name, trading_name, ABN/ACN checksum branches, state, postcode and country all match their ontology targets, and placeholders ('0', ACN-shaped or 11-digit values in the wrong rule) are filtered correctly. The main substantive doubt is the address group: CRED_LIC_LOCALITY/STATE/PCODE are labelled claim_scope 'licence_holder_address' although the supplied publisher evidence says nothing about address kind, and ASIC extracts can carry premises addresses, so the scope is asserted rather than evidenced (rule 4 doubtful; rules 5-6 acceptable on data quality). The unmapped list is well justified: licence number, licence start/end dates, licence status and AFSL number are licence attributes, not entity identifiers, dates or status, and mapping CRED_LIC_START_DT to entity.date_registered was correctly avoided. The clearest gap is entity_type: the register's registered-name suffixes ('PTY LTD', 'LIMITED') and individual personal-name entries are direct evidence available but unused.

publisher_evidence.notes: The credit licence is maintained separately from the holder's business registration. Changes to a credit licence name follow updates to the business register. Grant, suspension and cancellation dates concern the licence.
